'''Gillian Thornley''' is a retired New Zealander mathematician.

Gillian Brown Thornley was born in 1940 in [[Murchison, New Zealand|Murchison]], New Zealand.  Living on the family dairy farm,<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Hendy|first=Mike|title=Gillian Thornley|url=https://nzmathsoc.org.nz/downloads/profiles/NZMSprofile71_Gillian_Thornley.pdf?t=1263167969|journal=New Zealand Mathematical Society Newsletter |issue=71 |access-date=20 November 2024}}</ref> she won a scholarship to board at [[Nelson College for Girls]] and in 1958 enrolled at [[University of Canterbury|Canterbury University]] where she graduated with a masters with first class honours in mathematics in 1963.  At Canterbury she was a contemporary of [[Beatrice Tinsley]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=Women Sum It Up: Biographical Sketches of Women Mathematicians |first1=Diane|last1=Farquhar |first2=Mary-Rose |last2=Lynn |date=1989|publisher=Hazard Press|isbn=0908790066|location=Christchurch, N.Z.|pages=72–73|oclc=23448330}}</ref>

==Academic career== 
Thornley  received her PhD in metric differential geometry from the University of Toronto in 1963.  She returned first to Canterbury then took up a two-year lectureship in Trinidad at the University of The West Indies.  She then moved back to New Zealand (Nelson and Wellington), combining part-time positions in both academia and the public service (where she worked on economic modelling)  with caring for her two young children.<ref name=":0" />  She joined the mathematics institute at [[Massey University]], Palmerston North, remaining there from 1980 to her retirement in 2006.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nzmathsoc.org.nz|title=NZMS newsletter, Dec 2005}}</ref> In 1989 she was elected first woman President of the [[New Zealand Mathematical Society]]. Thornley presented at the 1990 Conference of the International Mathematics Organisation on the experience of women mathematicians in academia.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Complexities : women in mathematics|title-link= Complexities: Women in Mathematics |date=2005|publisher=Princeton University Press|editor1=Case, Bettye Anne|editor1-link=Bettye Anne Case|editor2=Leggett, Anne M.|editor2-link=Anne M. Leggett|isbn=1400880165|location=Princeton, N.J.|pages=140|oclc=949753960}}</ref> She also co-authored an article in 2001 on the experience of mathematics doctoral students in New Zealand.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Morton|first1=Margaret|last2=Thornley|first2=Gillian|date=2001-06-01|title=Experiences of Doctoral Students in Mathematics in New Zealand|journal=Assessment & Evaluation in Higher Education|volume=26|issue=2|pages=113–126|doi=10.1080/02602930020018953|s2cid=145702939 |issn=0260-2938|hdl=2292/4995|hdl-access=free}}</ref>

The Gillian Thornley Award was inaugurated by the New Zealand Mathematical Society in her honour in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Awards and Prizes |url=https://nzmathsoc.org.nz/?awards |access-date=2024-10-16 |website=New Zealand Mathematical Society}}</ref>

==Selected works==
[[File:Linear Geometry and Algebra text by Gillian Thornley and Michael Hendy.jpg|thumb]]
* Gillian Thornley and Michael Hendy. "Geometry & Linear Algebra an introduction in two and three dimensions". The Dunmore Press Limited. {{ISBN|0864690533}} (1986).
* Knight, Gordon, Greg Arnold, Michael Carter, Peter Kelly, and Gillian Thornley. "The mathematical needs of school leavers." Journal issue 1 (1994).
* Morton, Margaret, and Gillian Thornley. "Experiences of doctoral students in mathematics in New Zealand." Assessment & Evaluation in Higher Education 26, no. 2 (2001): 113–126.
* Senarath, Padma, and Gillian M. Thornley. Locally Projectively Flat Finsler Spaces with ([alpha],[beta])-metrics. Institute of Fundamental Sciences, Massey University, 2004.
